title: Peanut Butter Banana Recovery Shake
seoTitle: Peanut Butter Banana Recovery Shake | Firefighter Smoothie
subtitle: Recovery · Recovery
description: Banana and peanut butter are the hall’s answer to a recovery shake that does not taste like chalk. Frozen banana keeps the texture thick without needing ice cream or sweetened yogurt.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Peanut Butter Banana Recovery Shake in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on. Use cocoa powder as listed — measure each before heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch Protein blend. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Break frozen banana slices
steps.instruction: Break frozen banana slices apart and add to the blender with peanut butter, milk, yogurt, and salt. Serve cold within 10 minutes — hold blended cups on ice at 38°F if the line runs long. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Blend on high 60–90
steps.instruction: Blend on high 60–90 seconds, stopping once to scrape down the sides if the blade stalls. Serve cold within 10 minutes — hold blended cups on ice at 38°F if the line runs long. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: The shake should be
steps.instruction: The shake should be thick enough to coat a spoon and slowly fall off — add ¼ cup milk if your blender struggles. Serve cold within 10 minutes — hold blended cups on ice at 38°F if the line runs long. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Pour into cups right
steps.instruction: Pour into cups right away; this one thickens as it sits. Serve cold within 10 minutes — hold blended cups on ice at 38°F if the line runs long. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.
